_byte_base: Dn is data[n]. The source table is the community BMW Motorrad CAN sheet, whose Key tab defines the payload as D0..D7; its 2013 ancestor numbered the same fields byte1..byte8, and the K25 Arduino sniffer built from that ancestor reads heated grips from data[7] and throttle from data[1], which is D7 and D1 here. Set to 1 only for a table written with D1 meaning data[0].
_sources: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1tUrOES5fQZa92Robr6uP8v2dzQDq9ohHjUiTU3isqdc (BMW Motorrad CAN messages, Keith Conger et al.)
https://github.com/4G-Gregg/BMW-GS-CAN-Sniffer (2010 R1200GS, Arduino; Event_Printer.ino is the ground truth for what actually ran on a K25)
_extraction: bytes[] is little-endian, least-significant first: (D3*256+D2) is bytes:[2,3]. nibble is 'high' or 'low'. value = raw*scale + offset. map keys are uppercase hex of the extracted value; 'default' labels any code not in the map, otherwise it reports as unmapped_0xNN. deadband/min_ms suppress chatter on analog signals.

signals.name: clutch_kill
signals._note: Both sheet generations say the HIGH nibble of D4. The Arduino sniffer reads the LOW nibble of data[4] for the same 6/A values. Unresolved: pull the clutch and watch which nibble of D4 moves in /can/dump.

signals.name: asc_abs
signals._note: Sheet and Arduino sniffer agree: low nibble of D5, 5/6.

signals.name: throttle_pct
signals._note: The current sheet says D6(High Nibble) with a /255 formula. The 2013 sheet listed this as whole byte 7 (D6) with the same formula and the K50 row uses a whole byte too; the nibble label is a later transcription slip. Whole byte used. Should track throttle_valve_pct.

signals.name: high_beam
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: LO_NIBBLE(data[6]), 9 on / A off.

signals.name: turn_signals
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: whole data[7].

signals.name: abs
signals._note: Sheet says LOW nibble of D1. The Arduino sniffer reads HI_NIBBLE(data[1]) for the same 5/B values. Unresolved; cycle ABS off and watch D1.

signals.name: front_wheel_speed_kmh
signals._note: The ~0.06 dates from the original 2013 entry and was never firmed up. No GPS needed: at steady speed in a straight line front and rear must agree, so scale = 0.06 * rear_raw / front_raw. Adjust here once measured.

signals.name: brake_levers
signals._note: Two encodings: static values (03/07/0B/0F) and, after two full wheel revolutions, in-motion values (00/04/08/0C). Both folded into one map since the values do not collide. The Arduino sniffer reads the low nibble with 3/7/B, which is the same thing.

signals.name: gear
signals._note: The 2013 sheet said the LOW nibble; the current sheet says HIGH, attributed to eight models including the K25, and assigns the low nibble to an oil-level fault flag. High nibble used.

signals.name: info_button
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: LO_NIBBLE(data[5]), 5 short / 6 long.

signals.name: heated_grips
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: HI_NIBBLE(data[7]), C/D/E. F is the whole-byte FF the ZFE sends with the ignition off, so it is labelled rather than reported as unmapped.

signals.name: ignition
signals._note: The sheet's FF=Off/DF=On row was contributed for the K25 and F800GSA and its 'DF' is simply the grips-low value with a fixed low nibble; it does not contradict heated_grips, it observed the same byte with the grips on low. Encoded as: FF means off, any other value means on.

signals.name: ambient_light
signals._note: Sheet: B dark, 7 light, 3 and F unknown. The Arduino sniffer used 7 dark, 3 light. Unmapped codes will surface as unmapped_0xN; record what the bike sends in the dark and in sunlight.

signals.name: counter
signals._note: Purpose unidentified in the source table.

signals.name: odometer_km_alt
signals._note: Second odometer copy; cross-check against 3F8 odometer_km.

signals.name: countdown
signals._note: Source lists no formula. Raw byte, published for identification.
